questions.question: For which nonempty sets $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ is it guaranteed that every point $\boldsymbol{p}\in\mathbb{R}^2$ has exactly one nearest point in $V$ in Euclidean distance?
options: Every compact set $V$.
Every bounded convex set $V$.
Every closed convex set $V$.
Every convex set $V$ with nonempty interior.

questions.question: Let $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be nonempty, closed and convex, $\boldsymbol{p}\notin V$, and $\boldsymbol{q}$ the nearest point of $V$ to $\boldsymbol{p}$. The nearest point satisfies $(\boldsymbol{p}-\boldsymbol{q})^{\top}(\boldsymbol{x}-\boldsymbol{q})\leq0$ for all $\boldsymbol{x}\in V$. What does this say geometrically for each $\boldsymbol{x}\in V$ with $\boldsymbol{x}\neq\boldsymbol{q}$?
options: The angle between $\boldsymbol{p}-\boldsymbol{q}$ and $\boldsymbol{x}-\boldsymbol{q}$ is at least $90^{\circ}$.
The angle between $\boldsymbol{p}-\boldsymbol{q}$ and $\boldsymbol{x}-\boldsymbol{q}$ is at most $90^{\circ}$.
The angle between $\boldsymbol{p}-\boldsymbol{q}$ and $\boldsymbol{x}-\boldsymbol{q}$ is exactly $90^{\circ}$.
The angle between the position vectors $\boldsymbol{p}$ and $\boldsymbol{x}$ is at least $90^{\circ}$.

questions.question: Let $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be nonempty, closed and convex, possibly unbounded, and $\boldsymbol{p}\notin V$. To prove that a nearest point exists, take $\boldsymbol{x}_k\in V$ with $\|\boldsymbol{x}_k-\boldsymbol{p}\|\to\operatorname{dist}(\boldsymbol{p},V)$. Why does $(\boldsymbol{x}_k)$ have a convergent subsequence?
options: Because $V$ is closed, every sequence in $V$ has a convergent subsequence.
Because $V$ is convex, the sequence $(\boldsymbol{x}_k)$ is monotone and so converges.
Because $\operatorname{dist}(\boldsymbol{p},V)>0$, the terms stay away from $\boldsymbol{p}$ and so lie in a bounded set.
Because its terms eventually lie in a closed ball around $\boldsymbol{p}$, Bolzano–Weierstrass applies.

questions.question: Let $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be a nonempty closed convex set and let $\boldsymbol{p}\in V$. Which statement about the points of $V$ nearest to $\boldsymbol{p}$ in Euclidean distance holds for every such $V$ and $\boldsymbol{p}$?
options: The nearest point is the point of the boundary $\partial V$ closest to $\boldsymbol{p}$.
The nearest point is $\boldsymbol{p}$ itself, and $\operatorname{dist}(\boldsymbol{p},V)=0$.
A nearest point exists, but it need not be unique when $\boldsymbol{p}\in\partial V$.
The nearest point $\boldsymbol{q}$ is $\boldsymbol{p}$, and the hyperplane with normal $\boldsymbol{p}-\boldsymbol{q}$ supports $V$ at $\boldsymbol{q}$.

questions.question: Let $V$ be a linear subspace of $\mathbb{R}^n$, let $\boldsymbol{p}\notin V$ and let $\boldsymbol{q}\in V$. Which condition is equivalent to $(\boldsymbol{p}-\boldsymbol{q})^{\top}(\boldsymbol{x}-\boldsymbol{q})\leq0$ for all $\boldsymbol{x}\in V$, for every such $V$, $\boldsymbol{p}$ and $\boldsymbol{q}$?
options: $\boldsymbol{p}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}=0$ for all $\boldsymbol{x}\in V$
$\boldsymbol{q}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}=0$ for all $\boldsymbol{x}\in V$
$(\boldsymbol{p}-\boldsymbol{q})^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}=0$ for all $\boldsymbol{x}\in V$
$(\boldsymbol{p}-\boldsymbol{q})^{\top}\boldsymbol{p}=0$

questions.question: Let $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon(x_1-1)^2+(x_2+1)^2\leq4\}$, the closed disc with centre $(1,-1)$ and radius $2$, and $\boldsymbol{p}=(4,3)$. What is the nearest point of $V$ to $\boldsymbol{p}$?
options: $\left(\frac{8}{5},\frac{6}{5}\right)$
$\left(\frac{11}{5},\frac{3}{5}\right)$
$\left(\frac{14}{5},\frac{7}{5}\right)$

questions.question: Let $V=[0,3]\times[-1,1]\times[2,5]\subseteq\mathbb{R}^3$, a closed box, and $\boldsymbol{p}=(4,0,-1)$. What is the nearest point of $V$ to $\boldsymbol{p}$?
Let $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon x_1+2x_2\leq4\}$, a closed halfplane, and $\boldsymbol{p}=(3,3)$. What is $\operatorname{dist}(\boldsymbol{p},V)$?
options: $\sqrt{5}$
$\frac{9}{\sqrt{5}}$

questions.question: Let $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon x_1+x_2<2\}$, an open halfplane, and $\boldsymbol{p}=(2,2)$. Which statement about $\operatorname{dist}(\boldsymbol{p},V)=\inf\{\|\boldsymbol{p}-\boldsymbol{x}\|\colon\boldsymbol{x}\in V\}$ is correct?
options: $\operatorname{dist}(\boldsymbol{p},V)=\sqrt{2}$, attained at the point $(1,1)$.
$\operatorname{dist}(\boldsymbol{p},V)=1$, and no point of $V$ attains it.
$\operatorname{dist}(\boldsymbol{p},V)=\sqrt{2}$, and no point of $V$ attains it.
$\operatorname{dist}(\boldsymbol{p},V)>\sqrt{2}$, since the line $x_1+x_2=2$ is not in $V$.

questions.question: Let $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ be a nonempty closed convex set, $\boldsymbol{p}=(4,5)\notin V$, and suppose the nearest point of $V$ to $\boldsymbol{p}$ is $\boldsymbol{q}=(1,1)$. Which line is guaranteed to be a supporting hyperplane of $V$ at $\boldsymbol{q}$?

Let $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be a nonempty closed convex set and $\boldsymbol{p}\notin V$. A point $\boldsymbol{q}\in V$ satisfies $(\boldsymbol{p}-\boldsymbol{q})^{\top}(\boldsymbol{x}-\boldsymbol{q})\leq0$ for all $\boldsymbol{x}\in V$. What follows about $\boldsymbol{q}$?
options: $\boldsymbol{q}$ is the nearest point of $V$ to $\boldsymbol{p}$.
$\boldsymbol{q}$ is the nearest point only if $V$ is also bounded.
$\boldsymbol{q}$ lies on $\partial V$ but need not be nearest to $\boldsymbol{p}$.
$\boldsymbol{q}$ is only nearest among points of $V$ close to $\boldsymbol{q}$.

questions.question: Let $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ be a closed convex polygon with nonempty interior, $\boldsymbol{p}\notin V$, and $\boldsymbol{q}$ the nearest point of $V$ to $\boldsymbol{p}$. Which statement holds for every such $V$ and $\boldsymbol{p}$?
options: $\boldsymbol{q}$ is a vertex of the polygon $V$.
$\boldsymbol{q}$ is the projection of $\boldsymbol{p}$ onto the line of the edge nearest to $\boldsymbol{p}$.
$\boldsymbol{q}$ is where the segment from $\boldsymbol{p}$ to the centroid of $V$ meets $\partial V$.
$\boldsymbol{q}$ lies on the boundary $\partial V$, not in $\operatorname{Int}(V)$.

questions.question: Let $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be nonempty, closed and convex, $\boldsymbol{p}\notin V$, and $\boldsymbol{q}$ the nearest point of $V$ to $\boldsymbol{p}$. Put $\boldsymbol{a}=\boldsymbol{p}-\boldsymbol{q}$ and $H=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n\colon\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{q}\}$. Which description of $V$, $\boldsymbol{p}$ and $H$ is correct?
options: $V$ lies in $\{\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{q}\}$, and $\boldsymbol{p}$ lies on $H$ itself.
$V$ lies in $\{\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{q}\}$, and $\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{p}>\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{q}$.
$V$ lies in $\{\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{q}\}$, while $\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{p}<\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{q}$.
Every $\boldsymbol{x}\in V$ has $\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}<\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{q}$, so $H$ does not meet $V$.

questions.question: Let $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon x_1\geq0,\ x_2\geq0,\ x_1+x_2\leq4\}$, the triangle with vertices $(0,0)$, $(4,0)$, $(0,4)$, and $\boldsymbol{p}=(3,3)$. What is the nearest point of $V$ to $\boldsymbol{p}$?

Let $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be convex and $\boldsymbol{p}\notin V$. Suppose $\boldsymbol{q}_1,\boldsymbol{q}_2\in V$ satisfy $\|\boldsymbol{p}-\boldsymbol{q}_1\|=\|\boldsymbol{p}-\boldsymbol{q}_2\|=5$ and $\|\boldsymbol{q}_1-\boldsymbol{q}_2\|=6$. What is the distance from $\boldsymbol{p}$ to the midpoint $\boldsymbol{m}=\frac{1}{2}(\boldsymbol{q}_1+\boldsymbol{q}_2)\in V$?
options: $\sqrt{7}$

questions.question: Let $V=\{t(1,2)\colon t\geq0\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$, a closed ray from the origin, and $\boldsymbol{p}=(-4,1)$. What is the nearest point of $V$ to $\boldsymbol{p}$?
options: $\left(-\frac{2}{5},-\frac{4}{5}\right)$
$\left(\frac{2}{5},\frac{4}{5}\right)$

questions.question: Let $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ be nonempty and convex but not closed, and let $\boldsymbol{p}\notin V$. Which statement about points of $V$ nearest to $\boldsymbol{p}$ in Euclidean distance is correct in general?
options: A nearest point always exists, but it need not be unique.
A nearest point need not exist, but there is at most one.
A nearest point exists if and only if $\boldsymbol{p}\notin\operatorname{Cl}(V)$.
A nearest point never exists, because the infimum is never attained.

questions.question: Let $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be nonempty, closed and convex, $\boldsymbol{p}\notin V$, and $\boldsymbol{q}$ the nearest point of $V$ to $\boldsymbol{p}$. Suppose some $\boldsymbol{x}\in V$ with $\boldsymbol{x}\neq\boldsymbol{q}$ satisfies $(\boldsymbol{p}-\boldsymbol{q})^{\top}(\boldsymbol{x}-\boldsymbol{q})=0$. What follows?
options: Nothing: this cannot happen, because the inequality is strict for all $\boldsymbol{x}\neq\boldsymbol{q}$ in $V$.
$\boldsymbol{x}$ is also at distance $\|\boldsymbol{p}-\boldsymbol{q}\|$ from $\boldsymbol{p}$, so the nearest point is not unique.
$\boldsymbol{x}$ is strictly farther from $\boldsymbol{p}$ than $\boldsymbol{q}$, by Pythagoras at $\boldsymbol{q}$.
$V$ must lie entirely in the hyperplane through $\boldsymbol{q}$ with normal $\boldsymbol{p}-\boldsymbol{q}$.

questions.question: Let $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon x_1^2+x_2^2\leq4,\ x_2\geq0\}$, a closed half-disc, and $\boldsymbol{p}=(3,-1)$. What is the nearest point of $V$ to $\boldsymbol{p}$?
options: $\left(\frac{6}{\sqrt{10}},-\frac{2}{\sqrt{10}}\right)$
$\left(\frac{6}{\sqrt{10}},0\right)$

questions.question: Let $V=\operatorname{Epi}(f)=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon x_2\geq x_1^2\}$ for $f(x)=x^2$, and $\boldsymbol{p}=(3,0)\notin V$. Let $\boldsymbol{q}$ be the nearest point of $V$ to $\boldsymbol{p}$. Which line is the hyperplane through $\boldsymbol{q}$ with normal $\boldsymbol{p}-\boldsymbol{q}$?
